content:17df6a6c8c0eac4ddbaefa4ce0695c7d.english_reader_card: A construction company in Oldham has been fined £30,000 after a 25-year-old bricklayer was seriously injured when a floor collapsed at a house on Lynn Street in June 2024. english_fact_card.what_happened: A 25-year-old bricklayer was seriously injured when a floor collapsed beneath him at a house under construction on Lynn Street, Oldham, on June 4, 2024. He suffered fractures to his leg, hip and hand, required surgery and spent a month in hospital. The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) found the contractor, Oldham Business and Construction Management Limited, failed to properly plan, manage and monitor the construction work. The floor had been overloaded with concrete blocks and was not properly supported. Unsafe scaffolding, lack of fire alarms and inadequate site management were also found. The company was fined £30,000.

english_fact_card.who_affected: The 25-year-old bricklayer; the construction company Oldham Business and Construction Management Limited
english_fact_card.why_now: The company has been fined £30,000 following the HSE investigation, reported today.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Highlights workplace safety failures and legal consequences for a local construction company.

english_fact_card.what_happened: A 25-year-old bricklayer was seriously injured when a floor collapsed beneath him at a house under construction on Lynn Street, Oldham, on June 4, 2024.
